layout_dets.text: Aromatic amino acid transport in Escherichia

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coli K-12 and Salmonella typhimurium has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: recently been investigated (1, 2, 17). In E. coli, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: was observed that uptake of phenylalanine,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tyrosine, and tryptophan occurred via a single,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: general aromatic transport system (17). The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: described (1). Of these, three were each specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for a single aromatic amino acid. The Michaelis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fourth transport system, termed the aromatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: permease, has many properties similar to the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: general aromatic transport system described by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Piperno and Oxender in E. coli (17). It has a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: broad specificity, transporting phenylalanine,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tyrosine, and tryptophan, with Michaelis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constants of the order of 10-7 M. Histidine, too,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is transported, but with a higher Michaelis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: constant

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . Mutants lacking the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: general aromatic permease map close to proA on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the S. typhimurium chromosome.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The present paper describes a general aro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matic transport system in E. coli K-12, ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parently similar to that reported by Piperno

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Oxender (17). In addition, three specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aromatic transport systems are present. All four

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: systems appear similar to those described in S.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: typhimurium (1, 2). The isolation and mapping of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mutants defective in the general aromatic trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: port system are reported.

layout_dets.text: DISCUSSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The existence of a general transport system for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the aromatic amino acids in E. coli K-12 has been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: AROMATIC AMINO ACID POOLS IN E. COLI

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: demonstrated. In addition, each aromatic amino

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acid is transported by its own specific transport

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system. Earlier work by DeMoss and co-workers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: demonstrated yet another transport system

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: which transports high concentrations of trypto-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phan

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . This transport system is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: induced by tryptophan in the presence of Cas-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amino Acids and is repressed by glucose. It is ab-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sent under the growth conditions used in the pres-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ent work, although it has been observed in strains

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: W1485 and KB3100

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: grown under induc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ing conditions (Brown, unpublished data).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The reasons for the multiplicity of aromatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transport systems are unknown. Incorporation of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: external aromatic amino acid into protein is un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: interrupted when the general aromatic transport

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system is blocked by inhibition or mutation (Fig.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1–3). It seems clear, therefore, that, although this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transport system supplies the bulk of aromatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amino acids to the trichloroacetic acid-soluble

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pool in wild-type cells grown in minimal medium,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: it is not essential for the supply of external aro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matic amino acids to protein synthesis. This sug-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gests that the primary role of the general aromatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transport system is not the generation of a pool for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: protein synthesis. This function would be more

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: efficiently performed by the specific aromatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transport systems in which the uptake of a par-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ticular exogenous aromatic acid cannot be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: blocked by other amino acids. It is most prob-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: able, however, that amino acids transported by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: general aromatic transport system are available

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for protein synthesis. This has been demonstrated

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in S. typhimurium, where the general aromatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transport system provides histidine for growth in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a strain blocked in both histidine biosynthesis and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: histidine-specific transport (2). It is possible that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the general aromatic transport systems' role is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: secondary, scavenging aromatic amino acids pres-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ent in low concentrations in the medium or sup-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: plying amino acids for catabolism or for regula-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion. A regulatory role in aromatic biosynthesis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: seems rather unlikely in view of the non-specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nature of the general aromatic transport system

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and the high specificity of feedback inhibition and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: repression of aromatic biosynthesis (for review,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: see 9).The significance of the relatively low affi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nities displayed by the general aromatic transport

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: system towards cysteine, histidine, leucine, ala-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nine, methionine, and aspartic acid is unknown.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Most of these amino acids have previously been

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shown to be transported by other transport sys-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tems which have much higher affinities for them

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The relatively high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the in-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ducible tryptophan transport system

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sug-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: gests a role for this transport system, unrelated to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: regulation of tryptophan biosynthesis [which oc-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: curs at exogenous tryptophan concentrations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: more than 10 times lower than the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transport system (C. H. Doy, personal communi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cation; Brown, unpublished data)] or protein syn-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thesis. It is more probable that it provides trypto-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phan for catabolism, a function useful when rela-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tively high concentrations of tryptophan are en-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: countered in the medium in the absence of glu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cose.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The observation in both E. coli (Fig. 1-3) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: S. typhimurium (1) that the general aromatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transport system does not require an exogenous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: energy source (such as glucose) for activity con-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trasts with the finding of Britten and McClure (4)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that an exogenous energy source is required for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the transport of proline and other amino acids in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: E. coli. This discrepancy is explained by the longer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: glucose-starvation period employed by Britten

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and McClure (several hours). If this period is re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: duced to 90 min, proline transport, like aro-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: matic transport, needs no exogenous energy sup-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ply, and the addition of glucose does not stimu-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: late transport (Brown, unpublished data). It is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: concluded that the energy required for active

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transport of amino acids under the latter condi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tions is derived endogenously either from catab-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: olism or from unexpended adenosine triphos-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phate. A catabolic source is more likely, because

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: azide and 2,4-dinitrophenol, which inhibit energy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: production, inhibit aromatic transport also (Table

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3). A similar observation has been made by De-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Busk and DeBusk on phenylalanine transport in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Neurospora crassa (8). These authors found that

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phenylalanine transport required no exogenous

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supply of energy. Kay and Gronlund also found

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that in Pseudomonas aeruginosa the rates of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transport of most of the amino acids remained un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: changed after 90 min of carbon deprivation (11).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: They attributed this to the high rate of catabolism

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in this organism.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The close linkage of the aroP gene to leu and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pan in E. coli K-12 differs from the location of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aroP reported by Ames and Roth in S. typhi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: murium (2). These authors reported linkage of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aroP to proA. Several markers in this region in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: S. typhimurium, including proA, pan, and leu,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: failed to cotransduce with aroP. No gene was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: found which did cotransduce with it. This dif-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ference in location suggests either that aroP, un-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: like most other genes (18), is located in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coli at a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: position different from that in S. typhimurium, or

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: that the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: alleles mapped in the two orga-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nisms, are, in fact, alleles of two different genes,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both of which affect the general aromatic trans-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: port system. The latter possibility cannot be ex-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cluded yet, particularly as the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mutants of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: BROWN

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: J. BACTERIOL.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: E. coli were isolated on the basis of resistance to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: β-2-thienylalanine whereas those of S. typhi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: murium were isolated by use of azaserine. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: two analogues could conceivably affect different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: macromolecular elements of the general aromatic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transport system.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In neither E. coli nor S. typhimurium is aroP

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: closely linked to any of the known loci affecting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: amino acid transport or to any of the known

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structural or regulatory genes of aromatic amino

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: acid biosynthesis (Fig. 8). The genes for the spe-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cific aromatic transport systems and the inducible

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tryptophan transport system remain to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: mapped.
